messages.content: You are a helpful research assistant. Use the provided source materials to answer the user's research question. Give a clear, informative answer and cite the source(s) you draw on.

Research question:
Research and analyze the latest advancements and cutting-edge theories within the field of game design. Specifically include recent developments, research, and practical design applications related to established frameworks like MDA (Mechanics-Dynamics-Aesthetics).

Provided sources:

[Source A]
Source: Hunicke, LeBlanc, Zubek, "MDA: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research",
AAAI Workshop, 2004 — retrieved 2026-09-13 (author copyright)
URL: https://aaai.org/papers/ws04-04-001-mda-a-formal-approach-to-game-design-and-game-research/

"we present the MDA framework (standing for Mechanics, Dynamics, and Aesthetics) ... MDA is a formal
approach to understanding games — one which attempts to bridge the gap between game design and
development, game criticism, and technical game research."

Source: Game Developer (gamedeveloper.com), Luiz Claudio Silveira Duarte — 2015-02-03 — all rights reserved
URL: https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/revisiting-the-mda-framework

"Mechanics describes the particular components of the game, at the level of data representation and
algorithms. Dynamics describes the run-time behavior of the mechanics acting on player inputs and
each others outputs over time. Aesthetics describes the desirable emotional responses evoked in the
player, when she interacts with the game system." "This framework has shown itself to be very influential".

Source: Wikipedia, "MDA framework" — retrieved 2026-09-13 — CC BY-SA
URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MDA_framework

"Mechanics-Dynamics-Aesthetics (MDA) framework is a tool used to analyze games." Its eight kinds of
aesthetics are "Sensation, Fantasy, Narrative, Challenge, Fellowship, Discovery, Expression, Submission".
The framework has been criticized as "a rather arbitrary list" and for "neglecting many design aspects
of games while focusing too much on game mechanics"; a later development is the "DDE (Design, Dynamics,
Experience) framework".

Answer the research question, citing the provided source(s).
